title: Director Advanced Shipbuilding and Manufacturing Excellence
text:
**Job Summary** 
The Director, Advanced Shipbuilding & Manufacturing Excellence is Gulf Copper's industrial design authority and the leader of its continuous improvement program. The Director owns the production-system concept for each Gulf Copper site in Galveston, Port Arthur, and Corpus Christi, Texas: how work flows through the yard, how material moves, what equipment and tooling are used, and how the facility is laid out to support it. On the front end, the Director defines the production-system, equipment, and layout requirements that the architect/engineering firm and construction manager design to, and leads the selection of production equipment and tooling. On an ongoing basis, the Director leads the company's effort to continuously improve shipbuilding, ship repair, and module fabrication methods, tooling, work content, and productivity across all sites, and investigates and introduces proven advanced manufacturing technologies including automation, robotics, digital shipbuilding, and artificial intelligence (AI). The role supports Gulf Copper's growth into construction of U.S. Navy (USN) and U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) vessels, government and commercial ship repair, and distributed fabrication of ship and submarine modules.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

This position is responsible for the following: Other duties may be assigned.

**Production-System Design Authority (Front End)**

* Own the production-system concept for each site, including process flow, material flow, shop and work-station arrangement, build strategy, and facility layout, and hold design authority over these elements within the facility modernization master plan.
* Define and approve the production-system, throughput, equipment, and layout requirements that the architect/engineering firm and construction manager design to, and review their deliverables for conformance to those requirements.
* Lead the specification, evaluation, and selection of production equipment and tooling, including heavy lift and cranes, panel and block assembly lines, cutting and welding systems, blast and paint facilities, material handling, and ship transfer and launch systems, including trade studies, vendor evaluation, and total-cost-of-ownership analysis.
* Define the role and target capacity of each facility (newbuild, repair, module fabrication, outfitting, and support) and the production-system requirements needed to achieve them, as input to capital sequencing decisions.
* Translate target vessel classes and customer requirements into facility and process requirements, including ship size, displacement, launch and transfer method, assembly sequence, test and trials, and delivery.
* Work with finance, business development, and the Grants and Workforce Development managers to develop business cases and cost models for production-system and equipment investments.

**Continuous Improvement & Industrial Engineering**

* Lead Gulf Copper's continuous improvement program across all sites, establishing the methodology, governance, cadence, and reporting for improvement of shipbuilding, ship repair, and module fabrication processes.
* Establish and maintain productivity baselines and targets (such as man-hours per ton, cycle time, first-pass yield, rework, and schedule adherence) by site, product line, and process, and report progress against them.
* Lead value-stream mapping, work measurement, line balancing, and takt-based planning for fabrication, assembly, outfitting, and repair processes.
* Develop, document, and sustain standard work, production standards, procedures, and work instructions that reflect current best methods, tooling, and facilities.
* Lead cross-functional improvement events and projects with yard operations, engineering, planning, quality, and supply chain, and track resulting savings against investment.
* Operate a lessons-learned loop that feeds production experience back into layout, equipment, tooling, and build-strategy decisions.
* Set methods, standards, and tooling for the yards; General Managers retain ownership of daily production execution.

**Advanced Technology: Automation, Robotics, Digital Shipbuilding & AI**

* Investigate, evaluate, and benchmark new shipbuilding technologies and methods through industry research, domestic and international shipyard visits, vendor engagement, and partnerships with government and academic organizations.
* Develop business cases, pilot programs, and implementation plans for new technologies, and lead implementation of proven techniques such as robotic and automated welding, cutting, and panel and module production lines.
* Evaluate and pilot AI, data analytics, and digital shipbuilding tools for production planning, scheduling, quality, and productivity improvement, and scale those that demonstrate value.
* Work with engineering, IT, and operations to integrate new technologies with design, production control, and quality systems.
* Partner with the Workforce Development Manager to train and upskill the workforce to operate and maintain new methods and technologies.

**Module Fabrication & Distributed Manufacturing**

* Define the production-system and facility requirements for complex module fabrication, including large steel, piping, outfitting, and system modules for surface ships and submarines.
* Establish standard processes for module design interfaces, tolerances, dimensional control, quality assurance, transportation, and integration across Gulf Copper sites and outside partners.
* Define the production approach and facility requirements for a distributed manufacturing model in which modules are built across Gulf Copper's Texas facilities and with partners, then transported and integrated at the final assembly site.

**Leadership, Collaboration & Reporting**

* Lead the industrial engineering and continuous improvement staff and matrixed engineering, planning, and project personnel assigned to advanced shipbuilding initiatives.
* Coordinate with yard General Managers, engineering, estimating, supply chain, quality, and safety to implement new methods, tooling, and equipment and to prepare the yards for new shipbuilding and repair work.
* Provide facility, capacity, production-approach, and productivity input to business development, capture, and proposal teams for USN, USCG, and commercial opportunities, and serve as technical subject-matter expert on production capability in customer and partner discussions.
* Prepare reports and presentations for executive leadership on production-system design status, equipment selection, continuous improvement results, technology initiatives, and facility readiness.
* Establish metrics and systems for tracking production-system milestones, equipment procurement, productivity, and capacity.

**Safety & Quality**

* Ensure new facilities, equipment, tooling, and methods are designed for safety and comply with applicable environmental, safety, and permitting requirements.
* Design processes and quality systems to meet NAVSEA, USCG, and classification society standards applicable to shipbuilding and ship repair, working with the Quality organization.
* Promote a strong safety culture in the introduction of new methods and technologies.

**Key Measures of Success:**

* Production-system concept, layout requirements, and equipment list approved for each site by the dates set in the facility modernization master plan.
* Productivity baselines established for each site and product line within the first year, with annual improvement targets set and met thereafter.
* Documented continuous improvement savings tracked against capital and program investment.
* Pilot-to-adoption rate and realized benefit of new technologies introduced.
* Standard work and production standards in place and maintained for modernized processes.

**Required Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial/Manufacturing Engineering, Naval Architecture, Marine Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Management, or related field. Master's degree preferred.
* Minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in shipbuilding or heavy industrial manufacturing, including at least 7 years in shipbuilding, ship repair, or marine module fabrication.
* Demonstrated experience leading continuous improvement, lean manufacturing, or industrial engineering programs in a production environment with measurable productivity results.
* Demonstrated experience defining production-system, equipment, or facility layout requirements for shipyard or heavy industrial facility modernization or expansion.
* Strong knowledge of modern shipbuilding production methods, including modular and zone construction, panel and block assembly, outfitting, and ship assembly and launch.
* Experience evaluating and implementing automation, robotics, or other advanced manufacturing technologies in a production environment.
* Knowledge of NAVSEA, USCG, and classification society standards applicable to shipbuilding and ship repair.
* Strong project management, budgeting, and scheduling skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; experience with project scheduling and shipbuilding design and production software preferred.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent continuous improvement certification.
* Experience with first-of-class production-system design for a greenfield or major brownfield shipyard stand-up, including panel line or block assembly line design.
* Experience constructing large, complex USN or USCG vessels such as icebreakers, combatants, or auxiliaries.
* Experience with distributed manufacturing of ship or submarine modules, including submarine industrial base programs.
* Experience benchmarking production methods at domestic and international shipyards.
* Experience with AI, digital shipbuilding, digital twin, or data-driven production planning tools.
* Experience with construction management or general contractor delivery models for large industrial facility projects.
* Prior senior leadership experience in shipyard operations, engineering, or production.

**Working Conditions:**

* Remote position.
* Regular travel among Gulf Copper's Galveston, Port Arthur, and Corpus Christi facilities, and to customer, supplier, partner, and industry sites, including international shipyard benchmarking.
* May require extended hours to meet project, customer, and production milestones.

**Necessary Equipment Operation:**

* Computer skills: MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) and project scheduling software.
* Ability to review and use engineering, CAD, and 3D model information.
* Office equipment, including telephone, scanner, computer printer, etc.
* Personal protective equipment (PPE) required when working in shipyard areas.

**Special Skills:**

* Ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams and drive sustained process improvement across multiple sites.
* Ability to evaluate and champion new methods and technologies and drive organizational change.
* Ability to think strategically over a 3–10 year horizon while delivering near-term improvement results.
* Ability to have difficult conversations with internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to motivate employees and build a high-performing team.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to work under deadlines and schedule pressures.
* Commitment to company values, policies, procedures, and safety programs.

* An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.
